Important notices for players are sent by mail to the
"Breakers Mobile", the mobile device handed out only to the
players taking part in "Battle Live-G".

You can read your mail from [Mail] in the [Main Menu], or at
other times from the [Mobile Menu], opened with the START
button.

All kinds of notices from the "Battle Live-G" staff and news
of new stock at the Players' Shop will all be sent by mail,
so please check it often.

This is the staff of "Battle Live-G", the Gunpla Battle live
event.
Welcome to Gundam Great Front!

Gundam Great Front (GGF) is a large Gundam event held in a
"1/1 Life-Size White Base", built just for this event right
in front of the "1/1 Life-Size Gundam Statue" in Odaiba.

The main venue of GGF is a huge open space made from the
White Base's "Mobile Suit Deck", its front leg, and its
"Main Hangar", its body.

It gathers all kinds of exhibits that pour cutting-edge
engineering, IT and hologram technology that brings virtual
worlds into reality into one goal: "recreating the Gundam
world".

A "Large Mobile Suit Model" that moves just like the real
thing, a "Life-Size Mobile Suit Hologram Show" with giant
machines flying around, a "Psycommu Control Simulator" using
brainwave detection, and more: a real Gundam world no Gundam
fan has ever seen awaits you!

At the very top of the White Base, in the "Main Bridge",
there is the Main Bridge Observatory with a view over all of
Odaiba, and also the "Gunpla Battle Simulator" battle area
for "Battle Live-G", the highlight of this event.

Here, using the Gunpla Battle Simulator, the dream system
that "lets you fight with the Gunpla you built", selected
players will battle it out.

The theme of Battle Live-G is "new great battle scenes are
born without end". Use your Gunpla-building skills and your
skills as a player to put on battles that write new history
in the Gundam world!

Congratulations on being selected as a "Battle Live-G"
player!

"Battle Live-G" is one of the highlights of Gundam Great
Front: a live broadcast event using the Gunpla Battle
Simulator!

Only the players chosen in a strict lottery can actually try

■Mission conditions

　Each mission has "clear conditions" and "fail
　conditions". Check both carefully when you take a
　mission.

　In most missions, the only fail condition is "running out
　of time".
　Even if your machine's durability hits zero and it can't
　move, the mission doesn't fail as long as there is time
　left. You can sortie again (retry) and return to the
　front.

■Retry penalty

　However, as a penalty for retrying, the mission results
　take away as many runners as the number of times you
　retried.

　If you retry a lot, you may clear the mission but still
　be unable to make your machine stronger... so do your
　best not to get destroyed.

　The runners taken away are chosen completely at random.

■Rebooting allies

　In [Multiplayer] (Online), you can "reboot" an ally
　machine that can't move and has started its sortie
　countdown by going up to it and pressing ⑪.
　A rebooted player doesn't lose any rewards.

　And of course, when your own machine can't move, allies
　may come to help you.
　But helping carries a risk too, so it may be best not to
　expect too much.
　Play in a spirit of helping each other!

　You can learn what to do during a mission from the
　Operator's messages and the "Objective" shown at the top
　left of the screen.
　If you're not sure what to do, for example when the gate
　to the next area won't open, check the "Objective".

■Clearing a mission

　When you meet a mission's clear conditions, the mission
　is cleared and you move on to the mission results.

This mail explains the systems around "part break", a
feature unique to the GBS.

When player machines and enemy machines in the GBS take a
heavy blow, their machine parts can come off. This is called
"part break".

A "part break" causes all kinds of malfunctions in the
machine.

----------------

■When a "part break" happens to your machine:

　You can no longer use what the lost part does.

　　- Head: you can't lock on.
　　- Arm: weapons and shields on the lost arm can't be
　　 used.
　　- Backpack: you can't boost.
　　- Leg: you can't move. You can't do anything at all.

　Fixed-weapon option equipment that comes with the lost
　part can't be used either.

　　★[Important] If you lose a part

　　　You can get a lost part back in one of two ways:

　　　- Move to the part lying on the ground and touch
　　　 it.

　　　- Pull it back with the "Recapture Beam", fired by
　　　 "holding ⑯" while "standing still".

　　　If you lose your leg part, the Recapture Beam is
　　　the only way to get it back.
　　　Don't forget: "hold ⑯ for the Recapture Beam"!

　Once the part is back on, you can use what it does again.

----------------

■When a "part break" happens to an enemy:

　The enemy suffers the same kind of malfunctions for the
　part it lost. After that, it puts getting its part back
　first.

　If you defeat an enemy while it has a "part break", the
　parts left behind will very likely turn into runners.
　If there's a machine part you really want, go for kills
　after a "part break"!

This mail explains each parameter of your Gunpla (machine).

----------------

◆Durability
　　Your hit points. They go down when enemy attacks hit
　　you, and if they reach zero your machine can't move.

◆Physical Armor / Beam Armor
　　Resistance to physical rounds, solid blades and the
　　like, and resistance to beam attacks. Higher values
　　reduce the damage from those attacks.

◆Shield Durability
　　Your shield's hit points when you equip one. If it
　　takes more damage than this, the shield breaks.

◆Melee Attack / Ranged Attack
　　The attack power of melee attacks with the melee
　　weapon on your arm or with your fists, and of your
　　ranged weapon.

◆Capacity
　　The limit on the equip cost of the weapons, shield,
　　option equipment and EX-Actions your machine can
　　carry.

◆Equip Cost
　　The total cost of your ranged weapon, melee weapon,
　　shield, option equipment and EX-Actions.
　　You can't equip a combination whose total goes over
　　your Capacity.

◆Weapon Aptitude
　　Your aptitude for the five ranged weapon categories,
　　the five melee weapon categories, and "Fist" for
　　fighting without a melee weapon.
　　Weapons in a category with a plus value get stronger;
　　those with a minus value get weaker.

　　These values are set by the combination of parts on
　　your machine, but there is also a system that can
　　change them.

This mail explains the "option equipment" you can set on

----------------

In the GBS, which is built around swapping machine parts,

　- fixed weapons built into machine parts (such as head
　 vulcans)
　- weapons that come with machine parts (such as a
　 backpack's beam saber)
　- "portable weapons" and "recovery items" added from the
　 Players' Shop

are all treated as "option equipment" that the player
chooses and uses.

■Setting and using option equipment

　All the option equipment your machine can use is listed,
　and you can set up to six of them.

　　* Even fixed weapons built into machine parts can be
　　 left unset and unused. They then cost nothing to
　　 equip.

　Option equipment can be assigned to Up, Down, Left,
　Right, Up twice and Down twice on the directional
　buttons. In battle, select it with the directional
　buttons and use it with ⑬.

■Differences between types of option equipment

　Option equipment works differently depending on its type.

　- "Fixed weapons" have limited uses or ammo, but you can
　 refill them during a mission by picking up purple
　 items.

　- "Attached weapons", such as a backpack's beam saber,
　 can be used without limit.

　- "Portable weapons and recovery items" from the Players'
　 Shop have a set number of uses and can't be refilled
　 during a mission.

GAIOS, the AI-powered OS that controls your machine, is
known to learn "Expansion Actions" under certain conditions,
or sometimes "come up with" new ones on its own.

The GBS turns this into a feature the player can control.
That is the "EX-Action".

The first EX-Action you unlock, "Mirage Shot", is an attack
that creates two "virtual muzzles" to the left and right of
your rifle's muzzle and fires three beams in total. In
system terms it is close to a "cheat" by GAIOS, but it was
deliberately made an official feature to make the game more
fun.

Players who cleared the two tutorial missions also get two
more EX-Actions.

----------------

■Setting EX-Actions

　You can equip up to three EX-Actions on your machine.
　(But each one you equip adds to your "Equip Cost".)

　Which three you choose has a big effect on your battle
　strategy, so try all kinds of combinations and find the
　one that works best for you.

■Using EX-Actions

　Each EX-Action has its own charge time and can be used
　once it's charged.

　Once it's charged, use it with ⑯ + ⑫, ⑪ or ⑬ (the button
　you set).

■Learning new EX-Actions

　GAIOS has been seen to learn new EX-Actions when, for
　example:

　- you keep using weapons of the same category and "master
　 the weapon"
　- you keep using an EX-Action you learned and "master the
　 move"
　- you "get machine parts with special abilities" and it
　 analyzes them

　Keep these in mind as you play, and the EX-Actions you
　can use will grow.

■About Ace Points

　Certain actions during a mission add "Ace Points".
　Ace Points measure "how much you're contributing" in a
　mission, or "how cool your play is".

　◆Base points:
　　Added each time you destroy an enemy machine or damage
　　an enemy main machine.

　◆Ace Point bonuses:
　　Earned when you meet certain conditions during a
　　mission. Conditions for a bonus include "defeating
　　enemies in a row", "using certain weapons effectively"
　　and "causing many 'part breaks' on enemies". When you
　　earn one, a bonus medal appears in the middle of the
　　screen.

　* There seem to be other ways to raise your Ace Points
　 too...

　However, if your durability hits zero during a mission
　and your machine can't move, a set share of your Ace
　Points is taken away.

■Changes in a mission from Ace Points

　In some missions, reaching a certain number of Ace Points
　causes special changes, such as new enemies appearing or
　a door to another route opening.

■Getting decals

　Clear a mission with more than its set number of Ace
　Points and you'll receive a "machine decal" as proof that
　you're an ace.

　The decal you get is different for each mission, so try
　to collect the decals from every mission.

settings.

Your skill at building model kits suited to the Battle

Your Builder Level goes up as you keep making parts from
runners and gain experience.

However, making the same machine part again and again

　 functions of [Gunpla Paint] unlock, letting you
　 decorate your machine more realistically.

　Also, more kinds of parts become available in "Scratch
　Build", which makes different machine parts from certain
　runners.

The GBS, which scans the Gunpla you build into data so you
can battle with it, rests on two core technologies.

One is the ultra-precise 3D scanning system that "scans a
Gunpla and turns it into data, including its quality".

The other is the data control operating system that
"controls the Gunpla scan data as a 'machine' and moves it
directly according to the player's input".

The latter is the learning OS "GAIOS".

----------------

■What is GAIOS?

It stands for "Gunpla Artificial Intelligence Operating
System" ((For Driving) GUNPLA (Data) - A. I. - OS)... in
other words, "a learning OS that moves your Gunpla data".

"GAIOS Version 1.0", given to every player at the start, has
already finished learning the basics of machine control, and
can move machine parts without complex mechanisms as they
are.

The EX-Action "Mirage Shot", which GAIOS came up with on its
own while learning basic combat, and "Armor Repair" and
"Heroic Finish", recommended as standard equipment for the
Battle Live system, are also made available after the
tutorial missions.

----------------

GAIOS has the following functions.

----------------

■Basic control of machine data:

　As the base OS, it controls the basics of how your
　machine acts. It automatically handles posture control,
　such as standing, moving and recovering from damage, and
　fire control when attacking.

■Machine status self-check:

　It constantly checks your machine's status and tells you
　by voice about "system start", "EX-Action charged",
　"abnormal states", "low durability", "system down" and
　other information about your machine.

■Emotional reactions:

　For more natural learning, it has been given a little
　"emotion". It gets discouraged when things go badly and
　happy when you pull off a good move.

■Growth and expansion through learning:

　It has a powerful AI learning function and expands its
　own functions as it gains combat experience.
　When it expands, that is, gets a version-up, it can
　handle machine parts with more complex mechanisms.
　(In other words, more kinds of parts can be set on your
　machine.)

　Under certain conditions, it may also "come up with" new
　EX-Actions.
　For learning new EX-Actions, see the "GBS About
　EX-Actions" mail.

----------------

　Fight your way through the missions of Battle Live-G with
　GAIOS as your trusted battle partner.

Triggering "Awakening", an added function of GAIOS, greatly
boosts your machine's abilities, with all of the following
effects at once.

----------------

■Faster actions:

　Your machine acts faster overall. Step distance and boost
　speed go up too.

■Automatic durability recovery:

　Your durability keeps recovering during Awakening. Awaken
　when your durability is low, and this recovery can get
　you out of a pinch.

■No flinching or knockback:

　Enemy attacks no longer make you "flinch" or "get knocked
　back".

■Wider melee attacks:

　Attacks with melee weapons are enlarged, greatly widening
　their range.

■More shots in a row:

　The number of shots your ranged weapon can fire in a row
　doubles, allowing continuous fire.

■Option equipment (blue) recovery:

　The uses of fixed-weapon option equipment built into your
　machine parts, that is, option equipment (blue), recover
　automatically over time.

■Shorter EX-Action charge times:

　EX-Action charge times are shortened, letting you unleash
　powerful moves one after another.

----------------

A summary of things to watch out for in machine setup.

----------------

■Option equipment:

　If you set option equipment that comes with one of your
　machine's parts and then remove that machine part, the
　option equipment is removed automatically too.

■[Caution] EX-Actions:

　If you have an EX-Action set that uses your equipped
　weapon, such as "Mirage Shot", which uses a rifle-type
　ranged weapon, unequipping that weapon also automatically
　unequips that EX-Action.

　Likewise, for EX-Actions that need a certain machine
　part, removing that machine part also automatically
　unequips that EX-Action.

Be especially careful when you rebuild your machine parts or
change weapons after setting option equipment or EX-Actions.

----------------

■Gatling guns with shields:

　Gatling guns with a built-in shield, such as the "Gatling
　Shield", can't be equipped together with another shield.
　However, just equipping the weapon lets you "Shield
　Guard".

----------------

■Ranged/melee weapons:

　For weapons that work both as ranged and as melee
　weapons, such as "Beam Rifle (Zeta)" (base form) and
　"Long Beam Saber" (alternate form of "Beam Rifle
　(Zeta)"), unequipping the base-form weapon while both are
　equipped also automatically unequips the alternate form.

----------------

■Weapons/shields for specific machine parts

　If you have a special weapon or shield equipped that is
　only available while a certain machine part is set,
　removing that machine part also unequips them.

　This applies to:

　- "Beam Shield (Strike Freedom)", selectable with the

　- "Beam Shield (Destiny)", selectable with the Destiny

　- "Wing Shield", selectable with the ZZ Gundam Arm

　interfere too much can't be set on a machine together.
　This can happen with large parts such as the "Sazabi
　Arm", "Qubeley Arm" and "Qubeley Mk-II Arm".

The "Extra Mission Phases" in the Special Development Room
are made up entirely of high-difficulty missions.
The further you go, the harder they get, and more missions
are set to "No Re-sortie", so tough battles await where you
can't let your guard down for a moment.

Still, they should be beatable if you make your machine
properly strong.
Enemy units will include more and more MG machines, but you
can turn a crisis into a chance by getting machine parts,
weapon parts, Enhancement Modules and more from them.

Take on No Re-sortie missions only after making your machine
strong enough and fully equipped.
In Multiplayer (Online), the mission doesn't fail unless
every ally machine can't move. If you just can't clear a
mission, we recommend trying it in Multiplayer (Online).

----------------

■Tips for the Extra Mission Phases

- Every enemy attack is powerful, so securing a way to
recover with Enhancement Modules is a must.
　　Stack Enhancement Modules for auto-recovery, damage
　　absorption on hit, more recovery and so on, and don't
　　let your durability get worn down.

- If you lack the attack power to defeat enemies, you may
get stuck.
　　Get through by shortening EX-Action charge times with
　　Enhancement Modules, or raising your weapon aptitude
　　as high as you can to use the upgraded EX-Actions for
　　your weapon.

- You can get many Enhancement Modules in battles against
giant weapons (mobile armors).

- In "Multiplayer", make heavy use of "Armor Repair II" and
"Armor Repair III", which heal allies, to avoid everyone
going down at once.

- Plan your strategy from "your own means of attack" and
"what the enemy is good at", and judge well which enemies
to defeat first.
　　Charging blindly into the enemy army only gets you
　　focused down.
　　Work out which enemies to defeat first as you advance.

- In No Re-sortie missions, even if the mission fails, you
keep almost all the runners you got up to that point.
　　Keep trying and collecting parts; that is one way to
　　win too.
